scope: Contrast coverage, lexical depth, English reference varieties and next-language acquisition priorities. This is not a systematic exhaustive review or a measured revenue forecast.

answers.whyNot: Studies differ by learner L1, target variety, target position, task and use of words versus nonwords. A contrast inventory alone cannot certify a universal curriculum. Keep each literature connection and outstanding family explicit.
answers.minimumVocabulary: At least four distinct written word forms per sound category, aiming for five or more; also inspect compatible context groups. This is a product threshold, not a demonstrated optimum.
answers.english: Separate General American and Standard Southern British banks under one English product. The selected text bank has 27 American and 22 British contrasts; neither claims every accent or an exhaustive inventory.
answers.expansion: Owner selected Japanese as the ninth language for text-bank v1; it now has 10 contrasts and 100 words. Korean remains a later candidate. No new recordings are generated or pronunciation-approved.
answers.acquisition: Use the existing French and English search footprint while repairing all promised languages. Test new-language demand with an actually usable diagnostic once its words and audio pass review. Evaluate exercise starts, completions and subsequent paid conversion by target language and learner L1.
answers.revenue: No higher revenue forecast follows from a larger contrast or language count alone.

accentScope: Minimal-pair perception is one part of pronunciation learning. Word/sentence stress, rhythm, reduction, linking, intonation and transfer to speech require additional tasks and evaluation. Childhood clinical minimal-pair work is not automatically evidence for adult L2 accent acquisition.
